```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Widgets are not evaluated here so the built vignette stays small; run the
# chunks in R to see the charts.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
library(myIO)
```

myDAR maps a site from a phone walk. Each walk produces a point cloud, a DEM,
a GeoPackage with the track, GPS fixes and accuracy figures, and the device
trajectory. myIO reads those files into data frames and plots them.

## Reading a walk

`read_mydar_walk()` reads a walk output directory:

| File | Element | Reader |
|---|---|---|
| `walk.copc.laz` | `points` | `read_mydar_points()` (needs **rlas**) |
| `terrain.tif` | `terrain` | `read_mydar_terrain()` (needs **terra**) |
| `orthophoto.tif` | `orthophoto` | `read_mydar_orthophoto()` (needs **terra**) |
| `walk.gpkg` | `track`, `track_points`, `gps_fixes`, `pins`, `features`, `accuracy` | `read_mydar_gpkg()` (needs **sf**) |
| `trajectory.csv` | `trajectory` | `read_mydar_trajectory()` |

myIO does not install rlas, terra or sf; the readers ask for them when they
need them.

```{r read, eval = FALSE}
walk <- read_mydar_walk("path/to/walk", max_points = 20000)
walk
```

The reader keeps `max_points` of the cloud (every k-th point in file order,
which keeps the relative density across the walk; `Inf` keeps them all) and
records the full count. The DEM is aggregated when it has more than
`max_cells` cells. By default every table moves to walk-local coordinates by
subtraction: x and y become meters from the walk's south-west corner, z the
height above the lowest ground cell (`walk$origin` holds the shift). The
orthophoto comes back as a plain PNG with its extent in the same
coordinates.

The examples below use `mydar_iphone_walk`: a real outdoor walk recorded with
the myDAR iPhone app and processed with the myDAR CLI (autodar commit
`5f3aeb4`), shown in local coordinates only. Its x and y were moved to meters
from the walk's south-west corner and its heights to height above the lowest
ground cell, by subtraction only; the subtracted origin and the project CRS
are not included, and the orthophoto ships as pixels only. Classes, point
sigma, GPS residuals and the accuracy figures are as measured. It keeps 6,000
points for the SVG charts; `mydar_iphone_cloud()` returns 500,000 of the
walk's points for the 3D view. Neither needs the optional packages.
`data-raw/mydar_iphone_walk.R` in the myIO repository builds both from a walk
folder.

```{r walk, eval = TRUE}
walk <- mydar_iphone_walk
walk
```

A profile line across the middle of the track, used below:

```{r line, eval = TRUE}
ym <- mean(range(walk$track$y))
line <- list(from = c(0, ym), to = c(22, ym))
```

## The views

### The map: 2D and 3D in one view

`mydar_cloud_view()` is the walk's map, the way the myDAR app's Results
screen shows it: one view with a 2D / 3D switch.

- **2D** is the plan over the orthophoto, with a scale bar.
- **3D** is the point cloud with the orthophoto draped on the DEM, so the
  imagery and the points line up in one scene. When the walk has a mesh, a
  Points / Mesh switch shows the phone's scene mesh in its own colors.
- The **layer chips** switch on and off independently: LiDAR, Camera (when
  the walk has camera points), Classes and Ortho. Points can also be colored
  by photo color, height or sigma.
- The **track** runs through both modes with its uncertainty band, light to
  dark orange as the map-position uncertainty rises. The **profile line**
  and the **accuracy card** (Shape and Map, never merged) are on the map too.

Drag to orbit (2D: pan), shift-drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom.

```{r cloud}
mydar_cloud_view(walk, points = mydar_iphone_cloud(), profile = line)
```

The SVG views `mydar_plan_view()` and `mydar_orthophoto_view()` draw the
plan to scale (`setEqualAspect()`) where a WebGL view is not wanted.

### Terrain

The DEM uses the `raster` chart type: a grid of cells drawn as one image,
colored by height and shaded by a hillshade. Hover a cell for its height.

```{r terrain}
mydar_terrain_view(walk, azimuth = 315, altitude = 45)
```

The raster type works for any regular grid: map `x_var`, `y_var` (cell
centers) and `value`, and optionally `shade` (0-1).

```{r raster-generic}
grid <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 5, by = 0.1), y = seq(0, 3, by = 0.1))
grid$value <- sin(grid$x) * cos(grid$y)
myIO() |>
  addIoLayer(type = "raster", label = "value", data = grid,
             mapping = list(x_var = "x", y_var = "y", value = "value"),
             options = list(palette = "cividis"))
```

### Profile

Points within a corridor along a line, as height against distance along the
line, with the DEM height along the same line. `mydar_profile()` returns the
corridor points as a data frame.

```{r profile}
mydar_profile_view(walk, from = line$from, to = line$to, width = 0.5)
```

```{r profile-table, eval = TRUE}
head(mydar_profile(walk, from = line$from, to = line$to))
```

### Uncertainty and QA

```{r qa}
mydar_trajectory_view(walk)
mydar_gps_view(walk)
mydar_sigma_view(walk)
mydar_accuracy_view(walk)
```

`mydar_gps_view()` plots each GPS fix's residual against the fused track,
next to the 95% residual the processing expected. `sigma_m` is the per-point
1-sigma per axis that the cloud stores, on a log10 axis because camera points
(when a walk has them) run to meters while LiDAR stays near 2-3 cm; this walk
is LiDAR only. The accuracy chart puts the shape figure (how well distances
inside the walk hold) next to map position (where the walk sits on the map).
Here the map position comes from phone GPS, so it is far larger than the
shape figure within 5 m.

## All at once

`mydar_dashboard()` lays out the views on one page in the app's order: the
map first, then the profile, then the quality charts. In the map's 2D view,
turn on Select and drag a rectangle: the same points light up on the
profile; hover the uncertainty or GPS chart
and the other shows a cursor at the same moment (the GPS chart appears when
the walk has GPS residuals).

```{r dashboard}
mydar_dashboard(walk, points = mydar_iphone_cloud())
```
